1  [By Priyanka S.B .... Advocate]
 JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of North Women police station against the accused for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the accused no.1 married C.W.1- Shukoor Thahooneen Syed on 28.04.2006 as per Muslim rites and customs and after marriage, the C.W.1 begot three children and when C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 3 at the matrimonial home at Saudi Arabia , the accused no.1 to 3 harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally for no fault of hers and when the C.W.1 returned to India for the sake of children's education and was residing at R.T.Nagar,
Bengaluru, the accused no.1 failed to meet the C.W.1 and children and did not pay for the children's education and livelihood and harassed C.W.1 and thereby the accused subjected C.W.1 to cruelty
, therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused before the North Women Police seeking necessary action against him in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.29/2024 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded C.C.28620/2024 the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn,
after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, subsequently in persuance of summons the accused appeared before this Court and was enlarged on bail,
meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused , therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused no.1 to 3 in the language known to them, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 8 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

sentences.text: 6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
C.C.28620/2024 POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 married C.W.1- Shukoor Thahooneen Syed on 28.04.2006 as per Muslim rites and customs and after marriage, the C.W.1 begot three children and when C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 3 at the matrimonial home at Saudi Arabia , the accused no.1 to 3 harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally for no fault of hers and when the C.W.1 returned to India for the sake of children's education and was residing at R.T.Nagar, Bengaluru, the accused no.1 failed to meet the C.W.1 and children and did not pay for the children's education and livelihood and harassed C.W.1 and thereby the accused subjected C.W.1 to cruelty and thereby the accused no.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC?
2.
What Order?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the 'Negative'
 Point No.2 :

As per the final order,
 for the following:-
REASONS  9. Point No.1: 10.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Shukoor Thahooneen Syed and she deposed in her evidence that accused No.1 is her husband,
accused no.2 and 3 are the father and sister of accused no.1 and her marriage with the C.C.28620/2024 accused no.1 was performed on 28.04.2006 at Bengaluru.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused she was residing at the matrimonial house at J.C.Nagar at Bengaluru with the accused persons and they were living with together in cordial terms and accused did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.

Later she went to Saudi Arabia with the accused no.1 and stayed there for 13 years and even there also they lived a peaceful married life and accused did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that the accused no.1 and 2 are looking after the livelihood of the entire family.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused.

She deposed that when she had been to North Women PS in the year 2024 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any North Women Police Station vs Parvez Ali Bin Hashim on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184227382/
3 mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

sentences.text: She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

10. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the C.C.28620/2024 prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused , for which I answer point No.1 in the 'Negative'.
11. Point No.2:

In view of my findings on point No.1 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 3 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 3 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 3 are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 06th day of May 2025.)

(KESHAVA.K)
